theorem: For EVERY nonnegative diagonal weighted operator R on the eleven explicit generator vectors of the published 5x5 Schmidt-number-three grid, EACH of its 25 simultaneous coordinate cuts from 5x5 to 4x4 has Schmidt number <=2 whenever that particular cut is PPT. In particular, if R itself is PPT, every coordinate cut is PPT/SN<=2. This includes arbitrary nonnegative weights and singular boundaries. No assertion is made for non-coordinate cuts or arbitrary 4x4 PPT states.
source: Krebs–Gachechiladze, https://arxiv.org/html/2402.12966v1 Figure 2 and Appendix B. Let A=|02>+|11>+|20>, V=|01>, W=|10>, B=|12>+|34>, C=|21>+|43>, Q=|22>+|33>; the remaining loops are |00>,|14>,|23>,|32>,|41>. The original unnormalized state has all these eleven generator weights1 except the loops |23>,|32> have weight2; its trace is18, and source claims PPT/SN3. Independently, the checker verified its 25x25 PT is PSD. Write arbitrary weights alpha for A, beta for V, delta for W, b for B, c for C, and nonnegative weights for all other generators.
easy_twenty_one_cuts: If the deleted Alice row is 0,1,2 OR the deleted Bob column is 0,1,2, the projection A' has Schmidt rank<=2. All other source generators have SR<=2 before any local projection. Their defining nonnegative sum itself supplies an SR2 decomposition, independent of PPT. Exactly 21 of the 25 cuts are of this form; alpha=0 is trivial in all cases as well.
three_hard_cuts: For deletion (Alice,Bob)=(3,3),(4,3),(4,4), both |10> and the projected C'=|21> survive, and A' retains SR3. The partial transpose principal submatrix on |10>,|21> is [[delta,alpha],[alpha,c]], so PPT implies delta*c>=alpha^2. For alpha>0 this gives delta>0 and c>=alpha^2/delta. For z^4=1 let q_z=sqrt(alpha)*A'+z*sqrt(delta)|10>+conjugate(z)*(alpha/sqrt(delta))|21>. Its nonzero 3x3 head rows are [0,0,sqrt(alpha)],[z*sqrt(delta),sqrt(alpha),0],[sqrt(alpha),conjugate(z)*alpha/sqrt(delta),0]; the last two are proportional, hence SR(q_z)<=2. Their average is alpha[A']+delta[10]+(alpha^2/delta)[21]. Subtract it; c-alpha^2/delta is nonnegative and every remaining generator is SR<=2.
fourth_hard_cut: For deletion (Alice,Bob)=(3,4), B'=|12> and V'=|01>. The partial transpose principal submatrix on |01>,|12> is [[beta,alpha],[alpha,b]], so beta*b>=alpha^2 and beta>0 for alpha>0. Set q_z=sqrt(alpha)*A'+z*sqrt(beta)|01>+conjugate(z)*(alpha/sqrt(beta))|12>. The first two head rows [0,z*sqrt(beta),sqrt(alpha)] and [0,sqrt(alpha),conjugate(z)*alpha/sqrt(beta)] are proportional; SR(q_z)<=2. The four-phase average consumes alpha[A']+beta[01]+(alpha^2/beta)[12], leaving only nonnegative SR2 terms. The principal-submatrix statement is about the actual cut; it does not require the unprojected R to be PPT.
explicit_new_weighted_source: Increase the |01> and |10> loops of the original PPT/SN3 grid from weight1 to weight4; every other source weight stays unchanged. This adds product projectors to the original PPT state, and the exact 25x25 PT check independently confirms PPT. All eleven weights remain positive, so its range is unchanged; the source Appendix B range argument still forces the A coefficient of every SR<=2 vector to vanish. Since alpha>0 and the defining generators have SR<=3, this trace24 state has SN=3 exactly. Each of its 25 actual coordinate 4x4 cuts has SN<=2 by the theorem.

exact_checks.observed: The weighted checker hash-pins and replays the original all25-cut checker, then separately checks the trace24 weighted source PT and all25 weighted cut PT matrices by Gaussian/Fraction pivots. For each profile, it checks 25*256=6400 exact state entries, 16 individual four-phase rank2 vectors in the hard cases, and the trivial rank2 generators in all other cuts. The weighted hard-case phase coefficients are 2 and 1/2, leaving the exact nonnegative 3/4 edge weight. All checks passed. Universal weights follow from the written two-minor/phase proof.

limits: Coordinate deletions and the indicated weighted source range only. Non-coordinate 5x5 projections, generic 4x4 PPT states, high-SN witness existence, novelty, and independent/formal review remain open. The two source-range facts are attributed to the cited paper and not claimed new.
